newsitem.title: CHINA: Hainan and Zhengzhou top China's futures exchanges.
newsitem.headline: Hainan and Zhengzhou top China's futures exchanges.

text.p: Hainan's futures exchange and the Zhengzhou Commodity Exchange topped the list of China's futures exchanges in 1996 with both recording volumes in excess of two trillion yuan, officials said on Tuesday.

The Hainan exchange, in the southern island province of Hainan, was the most active exchange with annual turnover reaching 2.2 trillion yuan in 1996, up from 1.05 trillion yuan in 1995, an exchange official said.
The most active contracts on the Hainan exchange, formally known as the China Commodity Futures Exchange, are coffee and rubber.

The Zhengzhou Commodity Exchange, in the central province of Henan, came second with a turnover of about two trillion yuan in 1996, up from 1.19 trillion yuan in 1995, an exchange official said. Zhengzhou largely trades wheat and green beans.
Most of China's existing 14 futures exchanges saw a sharp downturn in business in 1996 with official restrictions on futures trading significantly tightened during the year.
